types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being. Also called individual, human, man, woman. Examples: Brenda Fricker, Phil Belfield, Christy Brown, Daniel Day-Lewis.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: exact match for the given definition and mentions

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

types.embedding_query_text: Movie: A film or motion picture. Also called film, picture, cinema. Examples: My Left Foot, Home Alone 2, A Time to Kill, So I Married an Axe Murderer.

chosen_type.label: Movie
chosen_type.justification: exact match for the given definition and mentions

mentions: So I Married an Axe Murderer

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: MovieClip
candidates.comment: A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment. Examples: a movie trailer, a deleted scene, a blooper reel, a short excerpt used in a review. Distinct from MovieSeries, which is a collection of related films.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A place or area. Also called place, area, site, locale. Examples: Dublin, New York City, Central Park, London.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: best match for the given definition and mentions of locations

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A group of people working together. Also called company, firm, institution, agency. Examples: CBS News, BBC.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: exact match for the given definition and mentions of news organizations

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: A day of the week. Also called day, weekday, weekend. Examples: Friday, Thursday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.definition: A unit of time representing a day of the week.
chosen_type.justification: exact match for the given definition and mentions of days

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Age: The stage of life at which a person has arrived. Also called years, age group, generation. Examples: 81.

chosen_type.label: Age
chosen_type.definition: The stage of life at which a person has arrived, represented by a numerical value.
chosen_type.justification: no exact match in schema.org, but Age is a common concept related to Quantity

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: TVShow: A television program. Also called program, series, show. Examples: Casualty.

chosen_type.label: TVSeries
chosen_type.justification: best match for the given definition and mentions of a TV show

candidates.label: TVSeries
candidates.comment: A creative work series dedicated to television broadcast and associated online delivery, comprising multiple seasons and episodes. Also called television show, TV program, broadcast series. Examples: 'Game of Thrones', 'The Office', 'Stranger Things'.

candidates.label: TVEpisode
candidates.comment: A single installment of a television series, typically part of a season. Also called television episode, show episode, broadcast installment. Examples: 'The Pilot' episode of a new series, 'Episode 5 of Season 2' of a drama.

candidates.label: TelevisionStation
candidates.comment: A local business or organization that broadcasts television programs. Also called TV broadcaster, broadcast station, local TV channel. Examples: 'WNBC (New York)', 'BBC Television Centre', a local news station.

candidates.label: TVClip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a television program. Also called TV segment, television excerpt, show clip, broadcast snippet. Examples: a highlight reel from a TV show, a news report segment, a commercial break.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Newspaper: A publication that contains news and articles. Also called paper, journal, gazette, periodical. Examples: The Guardian.

chosen_type.label: Newspaper
chosen_type.justification: exact match for the given definition and mentions of a newspaper

candidates.label: Newspaper
candidates.comment: A Newspaper, as a Periodical, is a publication containing information about varied topics, often published daily. Also called daily paper, news publication, gazette. Examples: The Wall Street Journal, The Guardian, a local community newspaper. Distinct from Magazine, which is typically published weekly or monthly with a specific focus.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: Article
candidates.comment: An Article is a CreativeWork, typically a written piece such as a news report, magazine feature, or investigative report. Also called written piece, report, feature, essay, column. Examples: a newspaper article about local politics, a magazine feature on travel, a scientific journal article, a blog post. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is a specific type of article published on a blog.

candidates.label: OpinionNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An OpinionNewsArticle, as a NewsArticle, primarily expresses opinions rather than journalistic reporting of news and events. Also called opinion piece, editorial, column. Examples: an editorial in a newspaper, a political commentary, a personal essay in the opinion section. Distinct from Report, which presents factual findings.

types.embedding_query_text: Book: A written or printed work. Also called novel, textbook, manual, publication. Examples: She Died Young: A Life in Fragments, her memoir.

chosen_type.label: Book
chosen_type.justification: exact match for the given definition and mentions of a book

mentions: She Died Young: A Life in Fragments

candidates.label: Book
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork consisting of a written or printed work, typically bound together and protected by a cover. Also called publication, volume, printed matter. Examples: "To Kill a Mockingbird", "The Lord of the Rings", "A textbook on physics". Distinct from BookSeries, which is a collection of books.

candidates.label: Audiobook
candidates.comment: An Audiobook is an AudioObject that is a spoken-word recording of a book or other text. Also called spoken book, recorded book, audio novel. Examples: a narrated version of "Moby Dick", a recorded lecture series, a podcast adaptation of a novel. Distinct from Book, which is the written text itself.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

candidates.label: Chapter
candidates.comment: A distinct section or division within a larger creative work, typically a book. Also called book section, segment, part, installment. Examples: Chapter 1 of "Moby Dick", the introduction chapter, the final chapter.

candidates.label: BookFormatType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing the physical or digital publication format of a book. Also called book edition type, publication format, reading format. Examples: "Hardcover", "Paperback", "Ebook", "Audiobook".

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: exact match for the given definition and mentions of a country

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: ITNonprofitType
candidates.comment: ITNonprofitType is a nonprofit type enumeration specifically for non-profit organizations originating from Italy. Also called Italian non-profit category, Italy NPO type, Italian charity classification. Examples: 'ONLUS', 'APS', 'ODV' (specific Italian non-profit legal forms). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a more general enumeration of non-profit organization types.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
candidates.comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.

chosen_type.label: Award
chosen_type.definition: A recognition or honor given for achievement or excellence.
chosen_type.justification: no exact match in schema.org, but Award is a common concept

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.
